reason: The low test tether is the only offered action and should keep the first flight contained.

effect: The whale is tethered; the landing cradle is the next available preparation.
reaction: A sensible safety step, though the result adds little detail.
reason: The cradle is the only offered gameplay action and should cushion the low test.
expectation: I expect to place the padded cradle beneath the tethered whale before lifting it.

effect: The whale now has a padded landing area, ready for the lift controls.
reaction: The safety setup is clear, though straightforward.
reason: The control lead is the only offered gameplay action and should let us operate the lift for testing.
expectation: I expect the lead to connect the lift controls so we can begin the low flight test.

effect: The lift works, but the dragon end is too heavy, so the balance needs adjustment before further testing.
reaction: The nose-heavy result makes the earlier balance warning concrete.
reason: The adjustment handle is the only offered gameplay action and should help counter the uneven load.
expectation: I expect to shift the counterweight to raise the dragon end, though the balance may need checking afterward.

effect: The counterweight adjustment has rebalanced the whale; it still needs checking.
reaction: The adjustment is straightforward, but I want to see whether it worked.
reason: The bubble level is the only offered gameplay action and should check the whale's balance.
expectation: I expect to use the level to check whether the whale is horizontal, though it may need further adjustment.

effect: The level confirms the adjusted whale lifts evenly; the emergency stop remains to be tested.
reaction: The contrast between the ordinary counterweight and the invented lift tile is satisfying.
reason: The stop cord is the only offered gameplay action and should allow the emergency stop to be tested.
expectation: I expect the cord and lever to operate the outside stop button and bring the whale down onto its padded landing area.

effect: The stop cord cuts lift immediately; a normal gentle landing instead requires gradually reducing current. The chapter goal is complete.
reaction: The distinction between an emergency stop and a controlled landing was useful and clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: The low hover revealed the nose-heavy load, giving the counterweight adjustment a concrete purpose.

leastWorthwhile.text: Setting up the tether and cradle was sensible but predictable, with only one gameplay action offered each time.

surprise.text: The emergency stop makes the whale drop rather than land gently; the padded cradle makes that distinction safe to test.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though the forced sequence left little room for meaningful decisions.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see the fair fly, though I would hope for more choices alongside the clear mechanism explanations.
